sentences.text: Only one fossil occurrence of Galeorhinus semiserratus has been documented.
The species was named by David J. Cicimurri, Jun A. Ebersole, and Andrew R. Bowman, who authored a 2026 paper in Rivista Italiana di Paleontologia e Stratigrafia.
Its type locality is the Tupelo Bay Formation, an Eocene carbonate unit in the outer Atlantic Coastal Plain of South Carolina, United States.
Sharks of the order Carcharhiniformes, to which Galeorhinus belongs, represent the most diverse group in the Tupelo Bay Formation, with twelve taxa identified.
Galeorhinus semiserratus is a valid species placed in the genus Galeorhinus, within the family Triakidae.
It belongs to the class Chondrichthyes, the cartilaginous fishes.
The species lived during the Priabonian stage of the Eocene, roughly 37.71 to 33.9 million years ago.
